items.q: All muscles of the pharynx are innervated by the pharyngeal plexus via the vagus nerve (CN X), with which sole exception?
o: Stylopharyngeus (innervated by glossopharyngeal nerve, CN IX)
items.exp: The stylopharyngeus is the only pharyngeal muscle innervated by the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX), derived from the third pharyngeal arch. All other muscles are supplied by CN X.
r: Correct. Stylopharyngeus is innervated exclusively by CN IX (glossopharyngeal nerve).
Incorrect. Salpingopharyngeus is innervated by CN X.
Incorrect. Palatopharyngeus is innervated by CN X.
Incorrect. Superior constrictor is innervated by CN X.
items.kp: Stylopharyngeus is the sole pharyngeal muscle innervated by the glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX).

items.q: Zenker diverticulum represents a posterior mucosal pulsion herniation occurring through Killian dehiscence. Between which two muscle components of the inferior pharyngeal constrictor is this dehiscence located?
items.exp: Killian dehiscence is a triangular area of muscular weakness located between the oblique thyropharyngeus fibers and transverse cricopharyngeus fibers of the inferior pharyngeal constrictor.
r: Correct. Killian dehiscence lies between the thyropharyngeus and cricopharyngeus muscles.
Incorrect. Space between superior and middle constrictors conveys stylopharyngeus and CN IX.
Incorrect. Area below cricopharyngeus is Laimer triangle.
Incorrect. Longitudinal muscles lie inside the circular constrictor coat.
items.kp: Zenker diverticulum herniates posteriorly through Killian dehiscence between the thyropharyngeus and cricopharyngeus muscles.

items.q: Which tonsillar tissue constitutes the superior component of Waldeyer tonsillar ring, located in the posterior roof of the nasopharynx?
items.exp: The pharyngeal tonsil (adenoid) sits in the roof and posterior wall of the nasopharynx. Hypertrophy in children causes mouth breathing, snoring, and eustachian tube obstruction.
r: Correct. The pharyngeal tonsil (adenoid) forms the roof of Waldeyer ring.
Incorrect. Palatine tonsils form the lateral elements in the oropharynx.
Incorrect. Lingual tonsil forms the inferior element at tongue base.
Incorrect. Tubal tonsils surround eustachian tube openings.
items.kp: The pharyngeal tonsil (adenoid) occupies the posterior roof of the nasopharynx in Waldeyer tonsillar ring.

items.q: During palatine tonsillectomy, arterial hemorrhage from the tonsillar bed most commonly originates from which direct arterial feeder?
o: Tonsillar branch of the facial artery
items.exp: The main arterial supply to the palatine tonsil is the tonsillar artery, which is a branch of the facial artery entering through the lower pole of the tonsillar capsule.
r: Correct. Tonsillar branch of the facial artery is the principal blood supply to the palatine tonsil.
Incorrect. Ascending pharyngeal contributes smaller branches.
Incorrect. Dorsal lingual supplies anterior lower pole.
Incorrect. Descending palatine enters superiorly.
items.kp: The primary arterial blood supply to the palatine tonsil is the tonsillar branch of the facial artery.

items.q: Which cranial nerve provides the sensory limb for the gag reflex, carrying tactile sensation from the posterior pharyngeal wall and tonsillar pillars?
items.exp: The glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) provides somatic sensory innervation to the mucous membrane of the oropharynx, mediating the afferent limb of the pharyngeal gag reflex.
r: Correct. Glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) provides afferent sensation for the gag reflex.
Incorrect. Vagus nerve (CN X) provides the efferent motor limb.
Incorrect. V2 supplies nasopharynx and palate.
Incorrect. V3 supplies anterior two-thirds of tongue sensation.
items.kp: The glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX) mediates the afferent sensory limb of the gag reflex, while CN X mediates the efferent motor limb.

items.q: The palatine tonsil sits in the tonsillar fossa, bounded anteriorly and posteriorly by which mucosal folds?
o: Palatoglossal arch anteriorly and palatopharyngeal arch posteriorly
Palatopharyngeal arch anteriorly and salpingopharyngeal arch posteriorly
Pharyngeal constrictor anteriorly and buccinator posteriorly
items.exp: The palatine tonsil lies within the tonsillar bed between the anterior tonsillar pillar (palatoglossal arch) and posterior tonsillar pillar (palatopharyngeal arch).
r: Correct. Palatoglossal arch is anterior pillar; palatopharyngeal arch is posterior pillar.
Incorrect. Palatoglossus is strictly anterior.
Incorrect. Uvula is midline superior.
Incorrect. Buccinator lies in the cheek.
items.kp: The palatine tonsillar fossa is bounded by the palatoglossal arch anteriorly and palatopharyngeal arch posteriorly.

items.q: Infection in the retropharyngeal space can spread directly inferiorly into the posterior mediastinum because the space extends down to which anatomical landmark?
o: Superior mediastinum down to T1-T4 (fusion with alar fascia)
items.exp: The true retropharyngeal space lies between buccopharyngeal fascia anteriorly and alar fascia posteriorly, extending from the skull base down into the superior mediastinum where alar fascia fuses at T1-T4.
r: Correct. Retropharyngeal space extends into the superior mediastinum to T1-T4.
Incorrect. The danger space extends down to the diaphragm, behind alar fascia.
Incorrect. Sternal angle is T4-T5.
Incorrect. C6 is the end of the pharynx.
items.kp: Retropharyngeal space infections track inferiorly into the superior mediastinum, predisposing to acute mediastinitis.

items.q: What type of epithelium lines the lumen of the nasopharynx, in contrast to the stratified squamous epithelium of the oropharynx?
items.exp: The nasopharynx serves purely as a respiratory conduit and is lined by respiratory epithelium (pseudostratified ciliated columnar with goblet cells), unlike the oropharynx.
r: Correct. Nasopharynx is lined by respiratory pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium.
Incorrect. Simple cuboidal lines renal tubules.
Incorrect. Stratified squamous lines oropharynx and laryngopharynx.
Incorrect. Urothelium lines urinary tract.
items.kp: The nasopharynx is lined by pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium, functioning as a respiratory conduit.

items.q: The auditory (eustachian) tube opens into the lateral wall of which pharyngeal compartment?
items.exp: The eustachian tube opens on the lateral wall of the nasopharynx anterior to the pharyngeal recess (fossa of Rosenmuller), bounded by the torus tubarius.
r: Correct. Eustachian tube opens on the lateral wall of the nasopharynx.
Incorrect. Oropharynx lies below the soft palate.
Incorrect. Laryngopharynx lies posterior to larynx.
Incorrect. Piriform recess is in the laryngopharynx.
items.kp: The eustachian tube opens on the lateral nasopharyngeal wall, surrounded by the cartilaginous torus tubarius.

items.q: Foreign bodies like sharp fish bones commonly lodge in which shallow mucosal depression located on either side of the laryngeal inlet in the laryngopharynx?
items.exp: The piriform fossa is a gutter on either side of the laryngeal inlet in the laryngopharynx. Pointed foreign bodies commonly lodge here, risking injury to the internal laryngeal nerve beneath its mucosa.
r: Correct. Piriform fossa frequently catches sharp ingested foreign bodies.
Incorrect. Vallecula lies between tongue base and epiglottis.
Incorrect. Fossa of Rosenmuller is in nasopharynx.
Incorrect. Tonsillar crypts are in palatine tonsils.
items.kp: Pointed foreign bodies frequently lodge in the piriform fossa, overlying the sensitive internal laryngeal nerve.
